name: kalshi-crypto-markets
notes: Structural gates over one `markets` pull of source kalshi-crypto (settled history). Structure only: every row arrives final (settled, yes/no), on a known series and strike geometry. Whether a market is usable for calibration (lead time, a quote to compare) is the model's call. Run: python -m dskit.onboarding validate --suite configs/suite-kalshi-crypto-markets.json --snapshot <snapshot-vid> --root <store root>. A snapshot holds one stream, so each stream has its own suite.

rules.notes: An empty pull is a broken pull (wrong series, API change), never a quiet day.
One row per market per pull; a duplicate means two status walks overlapped.
Each of the six series returned at least one settled market; a missing one is a ticker change or an empty walk. Six restates the series list; the pin test keeps them equal.
The six series the source pulls, RESTATED here on purpose: a suite must not read its vocabulary from the source it validates. tests/test_configs.py pins the two lists together.

A settled market reads yes or no. '' means unsettled and anything else (void, scalar) is a settlement the calibration test must handle by name: fail here so it is decided, then amend the suite (a new, auditable hash).

A value that is neither a known geometry nor empty is a new market type: block until a payoff rule exists. Known: greater, between, less (hourly) and greater_or_equal (15-minute up/down) were seen 2026-10-06; less_or_equal is documented, not seen. Empty is allowed here and WARNED by markets-strike-type-set. functional, structured and custom need a payoff rule before they can be calibrated, so they block.

An EMPTY strike_type is a market that was never given a strike: three real settled KXBTC15M rows from 2026-08 (KXBTC15M-26AUG080215-15, -26AUG101145-45, -26AUG140315-15) are finalized with a result, strike_type empty, floor_strike null and 'Target price: TBD'. They cannot be placed on a ladder: warn, then drop them by name; never guess a strike.

Strikes are USD prices of BTC or ETH, far above 100; a negative, non-numeric or sub-100 one is a unit slip (the history archive holds five such markets of 2026-04-13, see suite-kalshi-history-markets.json): read it before modelling.
As floor_strike, for the upper edge of a range or a 'less' market (the same unit-slip floor of 100 USD).
A market dated after it was acquired cannot be point-in-time.
